provider.name: Shopify
provider.description: Shopify is an e-commerce platform that allows developers to build standalone, embedded, and API-only applications using GraphQL and REST Admin APIs.

authMethod.text: Shopify uses OAuth 2.0 authorization code grant flow for standalone and API-only integrations, as well as server-to-server token exchange/client credentials.

difficulty.rationale: Registering a custom app or testing on development stores is fast and requires no external review. However, distributing a public app across multiple stores requires App Store review, partner registration fees, and compliance checks for protected customer data.

handsOnEffort.basis: Assumes a developer creating a Shopify Partner account, setting up an app entry in the Dev Dashboard, copying the redirect URI to/from Composio, and configuring required API access scopes.

summary.text: Custom apps installed in a single organization or dev stores require no review. Public apps distributed to multiple merchants require Shopify App Store approval and protected customer data access reviews.
summary.quote: Publish your app in the Shopify App Store and any merchant can install it once it passes review. A custom app takes the other path: one organization installs it directly, with no listing and no review.

triggers.text: Distributing an app publicly for multi-store merchant installations via the Shopify App Store.
Requesting access to Level 1 or Level 2 protected customer data in a public app.
triggers.quote: Public apps request access to protected customer data and protected customer fields through the Partner Dashboard.

publishedTimeline.text: Shopify does not publish an SLA or exact review duration in the retrieved documentation.

prerequisites.text: A Shopify Partner account to access the Dev Dashboard and create applications.
A one-time registration fee if submitting for public distribution on the Shopify App Store.
prerequisites.quote: Public distribution also requires registering for the Shopify App Store, which has a one-time fee.

redirectRules.text: The redirect URI sent in authorization requests must exactly match one of the redirect URLs configured in the Dev Dashboard or shopify.app.toml.
redirectRules.quote: The URL Shopify redirects to after authorization. Must exactly match a redirect URI you've configured in the Dev Dashboard or your app's configuration TOML file.

redirectRules.text: Redirect URIs must be valid URLs (using HTTPS for production web applications).

model.text: Scopes are provided as a comma-separated list. A write scope automatically grants its matching read scope.
model.quote: A write_* scope includes its matching read_* scope, so Shopify may return only the write scope. Treat a requested read_* as satisfied by its write_*.

examples.grants: Grants read access to product catalog and variants
Grants read and write access to orders and draft orders
Grants access to view orders older than the default 60-day window

steps.title: Start App Creation in Composio
steps.action: Open the Composio Dashboard, navigate to Auth Configs, select Shopify, and copy the provided OAuth callback/redirect URI.
steps.actorReason: The agent can look up the required callback URL format and guide the user through credential configuration.
steps.text: Initiate the auth config creation process on Composio to obtain the redirect URL required by Shopify.
steps.quote: For OAuth toolkits, the dashboard shows the redirect URI to add in the provider's developer portal.

steps.title: Create an App in the Shopify Dev Dashboard
steps.action: Log in to the Shopify Dev Dashboard, navigate to Apps, and click Create App (or use the Shopify CLI to initialize the app).
steps.actorReason: Creating an app requires logging into an authenticated Shopify developer account.
steps.text: Create the app entry to generate the public app record and credentials.
steps.quote: Dev Dashboard manages everything that belongs to the app itself: its credentials and scopes, your dev stores, user permissions, and its logs after merchants are running it.

steps.title: Configure App URL and Redirect URLs
steps.action: In the app settings (or inside shopify.app.toml), add the Composio redirect URI under redirect_urls and enter your application URL.
steps.actorReason: The developer inputs the redirect URL provided by Composio into the configuration fields.
steps.text: Enter the Composio redirect URL in the app's settings so the authorization code grant can return tokens successfully.
steps.quote: You've added your app's redirect URI to your app's settings in the Dev Dashboard, or to the [auth] section of your shopify.app.toml.

steps.title: Copy Client ID and Secret to Composio
steps.action: Go to the Credentials section under Settings, copy the Client ID and Client Secret, and paste them into your Composio Auth Config.
steps.where: Shopify Dev Dashboard > Apps > Settings > Credentials
steps.actorReason: The client secret is sensitive credential data that must be handled directly by the developer.
steps.text: Locate your Client ID and Client Secret in the Credentials section of the Dev Dashboard and input them into Composio.
steps.quote: In the Composio dashboard: 1. Click Create Auth Config 2. Select the toolkit 3. Choose the auth scheme (OAuth2, API Key, Bearer Token, etc.) 4. Follow the dashboard instructions for the required credential fields

steps.title: Save Auth Config and Pass ID in Session
steps.action: Click Create in Composio to finalize the auth config, copy the generated auth config ID (e.g. ac_1234abcd), and pass it into your runtime session.
steps.actorReason: The agent can wire the generated auth config ID directly into the application code.
steps.text: Save the auth config and pass its ID when initializing sessions with the Shopify toolkit.
steps.quote: After you enter the required credentials, click Create and copy the auth config ID (for example, ac_1234abcd).

agentPrepares: Determine required Admin API scopes and identify any protected customer data needs.
Format redirect URIs and draft shopify.app.toml configurations.
Wire the resulting auth config ID into runtime session code.
agentAssists: Guide the developer to the Shopify Dev Dashboard credentials and settings pages.
Walk the developer through adding redirect URLs and configuring access scopes.
humanOnly: Sign up or log in to the Shopify Partner account.
Copy and paste the Client Secret into Composio securely.
Pay the one-time registration fee and submit the app for App Store review if distributing publicly.

risks.text: Public apps requesting access to protected customer data (Level 1 and Level 2) must complete data protection review and state their data minimization justification.
risks.quote: Public apps request access to protected customer data and protected customer fields through the Partner Dashboard.

risks.text: Without explicit approval for protected customer data fields, GraphQL Admin API queries return null for those fields and return an error message in the response.
risks.quote: GraphQL requests to unapproved types will return an HTTP 200 Ok response with an error message in the errors hash.

risks.text: Secret rotation must follow zero-downtime rotation procedures; revoking an old secret before updating access tokens invalidates merchant tokens.
risks.quote: Don't revoke your old secret until you've updated all stored access tokens to use the new one. Revoking early can cause merchants to lose access to your app.

risks.text: Custom apps cannot use Shopify's app billing system to charge merchants.

unresolved: Published review turnaround times for Shopify App Store submissions are not detailed in the retrieved documentation.
Exact pricing amount for the one-time Shopify App Store registration fee is not stated in the retrieved pages.
nextActions: Navigate to the Shopify Dev Dashboard and create your app entry.
Retrieve your Composio redirect URI from the Composio dashboard and save it in your app settings.
Add your Client ID and Client Secret to your Composio custom auth config.
If accessing customer information in production, submit API access requests for protected customer data in the Partner Dashboard.

faq.question: How do I set up custom OAuth credentials for Shopify?
faq.answer: For a step-by-step guide on creating and configuring your own Shopify OAuth credentials with Composio, see [How to create OAuth credentials for Shopify](https://composio.dev/auth/shopify).

faq.question: Why am I seeing "App not found" when connecting Shopify?
faq.answer: The default Shopify OAuth app may be under review or expired. Use your own OAuth app or API authentication method until the default is restored.

faq.question: Shopify order update 403s can be caused by missing `read_all_orders` scope
faq.answer: Check the scopes on the Shopify connection. If order reads or updates require access beyond the default order scope set, reconnect with the needed order scopes such as `read_all_orders` before retrying.
